clue.text: Dyer knows it is proof against running at speed

definitions.text: Dyer knows it is proof against running
definitions.meaning: a dyer prizes colour that will not run in the wash, the quality of a fast dye
quickness or swiftness, the state of being fast

explanation.surface: A dyer explains that his colours resist running when moved quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast dye resists running, and the noun from fast also means swiftness, so one word covers both senses.

clue.text: He's fit to become an object of irrational desire

indicators.note: turned into something else, so the letters change into a new word

explanation.surface: A fit man becomes the subject of obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive fixation on an object or body part is an irrational craving.

clue.text: Brazilian dances for a medico in elite army group

indicators.note: placed within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the SAS, the Special Air Service, the British army's elite regiment
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, the qualification of a doctor

explanation.surface: Brazilian dances are performed for a doctor serving in special forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively dances of Brazilian origin, famous from carnival, are the national dance style.

clue.text: Epithet for a plutocrat not applicable to Australia's PM

parts.note: NA is the standard abbreviation for not applicable on forms
Bob Hawke, Australian Prime Minister in the 1980s, known as Bob

explanation.surface: A label for a rich man that cannot be applied to the Australian premier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Epithet for a' is link material leading to the definition. Bob Hawke was Australia's Prime Minister when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A very rich, ostentatious man, originally one returning from India with a fortune, is a wealthy person of power.

clue.text: The sort of court proceedings which call for a brief account

definitions.meaning: trial before magistrates without a jury, as in a quick court hearing
a précis or résumé

explanation.surface: A lawyer explains a kind of trial needing only a short statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick trial without jury bears the adjective, and as a noun the word is a short précis.

clue.text: Earthenware pots needing patient care

definitions.meaning: clay vessels, the pottery sense
invalids or broken-down people who need nursing, the informal sense

explanation.surface: Clay pots are so fragile they need careful handling.
explanation.definitionFit: Crockery is earthenware, and informally decrepit or injured people are called by the same word.

clue.text: Apparently the traffic project is successful-but not for long!

definitions.text: Apparently the traffic project is successful-but not for long!

parts.words: Apparently the traffic project is successful-but not for long!
parts.note: read as two words, a street that functions well; in fact the term for temporary repairs on a highway

explanation.surface: A traffic scheme seems to be a success, but only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as a phrase, it seems to say the route succeeds; really it is the repairs that hold up traffic for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Repair works on a highway are temporary operations that disrupt motorists.

clue.text: An eminent runner to run on and on

parts.note: to run on is to keep talking, to chatter
away as in 'talk away', meaning continuing on

explanation.surface: A famous athlete keeps going on and on.
explanation.walkthrough: Chris Chataway was a famous British middle-distance runner of the 1950s, a pacemaker for the first four-minute mile.
explanation.definitionFit: A famed British athlete of the 1950s who helped pace the first sub-four-minute mile was a celebrated runner.

clue.text: South Kew deer butchered and prepared for roasting-and his…

indicators.note: cut up like meat, so the animals named are chopped and rearranged

explanation.surface: Deer from a London park are butchered ready for the spit.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew is a district of London known for its botanical gardens; 'butchered' rearranges DEER into ERED. The clue runs on into 11-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat pierced on a spit or long pin is ready for cooking over heat.

clue.text: A terrorist's minute weapon?

parts.note: read 'minute' as a unit of clock time rather than tiny: a weapon set to go off at a chosen moment

explanation.surface: A terrorist is using a tiny weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' wants to be pronounced my-NEWT (tiny); read as MIN-it it points to clock time, and the device is timed.
explanation.definitionFit: A device rigged with a timer to explode at a set moment is what the time-based reading describes.

clue.text: Artist dining out may call for it if he wants…

definitions.text: Artist dining out may call for it if he wants…

parts.words: Artist dining out may call for it if he wants…
parts.note: a painter eating at a restaurant orders a jug of the house wine, as the next clue continues

explanation.surface: A painter eating at a restaurant orders something to go with his meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 12-across ('wine with first class meals'). There is a hint of RA, the artist, sitting inside CAFE, where one dines out.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass jug for serving wine at table is what a diner asks for when wanting wine.

clue.text: … does butchered for choice lines

indicators.note: chopped up like carcasses, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Female deer are slaughtered for the sake of fine poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems are pieces of select verse.

clue.text: … wine with first class meals-but not port

parts.note: a star performer or star turn is first class
board means meals provided, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Continuing the diner's order: wine with top-quality meals, though not the fortified Portuguese wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink after 'wine', but it is the left side of a ship; the right side is not port.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship the right-hand side is the opposite of the left side, which sailors call port.

clue.text: We've said how to make material

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the contraction is heard as a different word

parts.note: the contraction of we have, taken as the sound to be spoken

explanation.surface: Someone has explained how cloth is produced.
explanation.definitionFit: Interlacing threads on a loom is how cloth is made.

clue.text: Drama provides-little freedom of movement

definitions.meaning: a stage work, a piece for the theatre
slack or give in a mechanism, as in a rope with some looseness

explanation.surface: A stage show offers its audience a small amount of freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage piece is a theatre work, and a little looseness in a joint is also called by the same word.

clue.text: Sap rising in leaves, is all the homesick soldier asks for

definitions.text: all the homesick soldier asks for

indicators.note: placed inside, so one piece sits within the other
going up in a down entry, so the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Sap climbing in foliage is all a soldier missing home desires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' suits a down entry, where reading upward reverses the word; the plural 'leaves' is split around the inserted letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A document granting permission for time off is what a soldier longing for home wants.

clue.text: Ruse man employed to establish identity

indicators.note: used or put to work, so the letters are put to a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A trickster has been hired to prove who someone is.
explanation.definitionFit: A family name is what an official asks for when confirming who a person is.

clue.text: Dine on vegetarian substitute

parts.note: to sup is to have supper, to dine
plant food, as in plant-based, is what a vegetarian eats

explanation.surface: Eat a meat-free alternative dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the place of another, ousting them, is to replace or stand in for.

clue.text: Aninsular type who confesses to malicious gossip

parts.note: one admitting a fault speaks in the first person, I
slander is spoken defamation, spiteful talk

explanation.surface: A narrow-minded person admits to spreading spiteful rumours.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs 'An insular' together. 'insular' suggests narrow-minded, but here it means from an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from an island is literally insular, from the Latin for island.

clue.text: Steal the limelight, oddly enough by moving away from it

definitions.meaning: outshine others, draw attention to oneself
towards the back of a theatre stage, away from the audience and footlights

explanation.surface: Oddly, one can grab attention by stepping out of the spotlight.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor moving to the rear makes fellow players turn from the audience, so he outshines them; the word also names the rear of the stage.

clue.text: Nobleman Lear tortured

indicators.note: twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's King Lear tormented a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A British peer ranking below a marquess is a titled nobleman.

clue.text: Where things are cobbled together, but stand the test of time

definitions.meaning: a shoemaker's foot-shaped block on which boots are made
endure, go on, continue

explanation.surface: A place where things are hastily assembled but still prove durable.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler shapes shoes on a wooden form of that name, and the verb means to endure.

clue.text: Didn't go on-certainly not right on

definitions.meaning: stopped, ceased, as in 'we stopped where we finished'
the opposite of right on, the reverse of the side and position

explanation.surface: Someone stopped, and was decidedly not politically correct.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means stopped, and literally it is the opposite of right on in both words.

clue.text: The sound of a chiming bell-the first of eight

definitions.text: The sound of a chiming bell
definitions.meaning: a single chime of a clock or bell striking the hour
the oarsman nearest the stern who sets the rhythm for a rowing eight

explanation.surface: A bell chimes once, the first of eight peals.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock's single chime is a strike, and the rower setting the pace in an eight-oared boat is the stern oar.

clue.text: The first to take off a metal worker

definitions.meaning: the ... brothers, who made the first powered aeroplane flight in 1903
a maker or craftsman, as in wheelwright or shipwright

explanation.surface: The first to remove something is a smith.
explanation.definitionFit: The aviation pioneers flew first, and the word for a craftsman-maker survives in trades such as shipwright.

clue.text: Locality supplying soft dainty fabric

parts.note: p for piano, the musical direction meaning soft
lace is a delicate openwork fabric

explanation.surface: A district that produces gentle, delicate cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot or district is a location in the general sense.

clue.text: Astronomical instrument father found in a nuclear generator

indicators.note: discovered inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a reactor generates nuclear power
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A telescope's priestly inventor is discovered inside a power station.
explanation.definitionFit: A telescope that uses lenses to bend light, as opposed to mirrors, is an astronomer's tool.

clue.text: Take advantage of a tip

parts.note: vail is an archaic word for a gratuity or tip given to a servant

explanation.surface: Make use of a useful hint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like advice, but here it is the old word VAIL, a gratuity.
explanation.definitionFit: To make use of something, as in using an opportunity, is to profit from it.

clue.text: An ecclesiastical dignity from South American highlands

parts.note: a dean is a senior church dignitary, head of a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A church dignitary hails from the mountains of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for the great mountain range along South America's west coast describes things from those highlands.

clue.text: Why a vocalist may be employed cheaply…

definitions.text: Why a vocalist may be employed cheaply…

parts.words: Why a vocalist may be employed cheaply…
parts.note: the idiom for very cheaply, taken literally as payment in the form of one piece of singing

explanation.surface: A singer works for little money.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means for almost nothing; read literally, a singer would be paid for one tune. The clue runs on into 29-across.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at a trivial price, and literally it is what a singer is hired to perform.

clue.text: … a high-flying vocalist with a throat infection

definitions.meaning: a songbird, a bird that sings
candidiasis, a fungal infection of the mouth and throat

explanation.surface: A singer is suffering from a sore throat.
explanation.definitionFit: The song thrush is a familiar singing bird, and the same name is given to a yeast infection of the mouth.

clue.text: Very wealthy tributary

definitions.meaning: rich, well-off
a stream flowing into a larger river

explanation.surface: A rich river branch.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means rich, and as a noun the same word names a stream feeding a bigger river.
